name_note: Genomes GTDB places in g__Oscillibacter carry the NCBI names Oscillibacter or Dysosmobacter, so literature on Dysosmobacter welbionis describes members of this GTDB genus.

sentences.text: That type species forms n-valeric acid as its major end product from glucose.
A second species was isolated from the rumen of cattle and produces butyric acid as its major end product.
Dysosmobacter welbionis, described from human faeces together with an emended description of Oscillibacter, forms butyric acid from myo-inositol.
Across four human cohorts that species was detected in 62.7 to 69.8 percent of the healthy population, and was given to obese mice by gavage.
